task:
Create a NetworkPolicy to restrict egress from a frontend Deployment.

In namespace 'venus':

  Setup:
    kubectl create ns venus
    kubectl create deploy frontend --image=nginx:1.21 -n venus --replicas=2 --labels=app=frontend
    kubectl create deploy api      --image=nginx:1.21 -n venus --replicas=1 --labels=app=api
    kubectl create deploy db       --image=nginx:1.21 -n venus --replicas=1 --labels=app=db

  Task — Create a NetworkPolicy named 'np1' in namespace 'venus':
    - Applies to Pods from Deployment 'frontend' (label: app=frontend)
    - Policy type: Egress
    - Allow egress TO:
        * Pods with label app=api (ANY port)
        * UDP port 53 (DNS) to ANY destination
        * TCP port 53 (DNS) to ANY destination
    - All other egress from frontend pods is DENIED

Verify:
  kubectl describe networkpolicy np1 -n venus

Note: Without the DNS egress rule, frontend pods cannot resolve service names — always include port 53 in egress-only policies.
hints: policyTypes: [Egress]  explicitly sets this as an egress-only policy
DNS rule: spec.egress entry with ports [{protocol: UDP, port: 53}, {protocol: TCP, port: 53}] and empty 'to' (allows to anywhere)
api rule: spec.egress entry with to [{podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}}] and no port restriction (all ports)
Deployment label selector: app=frontend targets pods created by the frontend Deployment
detailed_hints: - to: [{podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}}]  # allow to api pods
- ports: [{protocol: UDP, port: 53}, {protocol: TCP, port: 53}]  # allow DNS anywhere (no 'to' field = all destinations)

validators.command: kubectl get networkpolicy np1 -n venus -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'
kubectl get networkpolicy np1 -n venus -o jsonpath='{.spec.policyTypes[0]}'
kubectl get networkpolicy np1 -n venus -o jsonpath='{.spec.egress}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('ok' if len(d)>0 else 'fail')"
